providers.description: Granite Construction is one of the largest diversified heavy civil contractors and construction materials producers in the United States, with operations spanning transportation infrastructure, water infrastructure, mineral exploration, and aggregate materials.

providers.name: Greenbrier Companies
providers.description: The Greenbrier Companies is a leading international supplier of equipment and services to global freight transportation markets, designing, building, and marketing freight railcars in North America, Europe, and South America. Greenbrier also offers railcar leasing, repair, and digital fleet management services such as RailPulse.

providers.name: Shift5
providers.description: Shift5 is an operational technology (OT) cyber and observability company that instruments the onboard serial data buses of planes, trains, and military weapons systems to deliver real-time intrusion detection, predictive maintenance, and compliance intelligence for defense and transportation fleets. Founded by former US Army Cyber Command engineers, it collects and analyzes data directly from vehicle bus networks (MIL-STD-1553, ARINC 429, CAN) to give operators actionable insight into the health and security of their platforms. Backed by Insight Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; enrichment confirms Shift5 publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Swiftmile
providers.description: Swiftmile is a California-based hardware and IoT company building universal charging and parking infrastructure for micromobility — docking stations that power, secure and organize shared and privately owned e-bikes and e-scooters, including solar-powered units and integrated digital advertising panels. Founded around 2014 and headquartered on the San Francisco Peninsula, it supplied secure charging docks to the New York City DOT public e-bike charging pilot alongside PopWheels and Swobbee. Company interviews describe a fleet- and battery-management backend with integrations offered to micromobility operators, but Swiftmile has never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and as of 2026-08-29 swiftmile.com no longer serves the company website at all — the domain answers with a Nexcess hosting placeholder and a TLS certificate that does not match the hostname.

providers.name: Bestmile
providers.description: Bestmile was a Swiss fleet-orchestration SaaS company, spun out of EPFL in Lausanne in 2014, whose cloud platform planned, dispatched and optimized mixed fleets of autonomous and human-driven vehicles for on-demand mobility and transit operators. The platform was described by the company as API-first, with documented Fleet, Booking and Transportation APIs for integrating operator booking apps, fleet-management systems and traveler-information systems. The company no longer operates: ZF Friedrichshafen acquired Bestmile's technology in November 2021 and folded it into its own SCALAR fleet-orchestration platform, so any successor API belongs to ZF rather than to Bestmile. As of 2026-08-17 bestmile.com is a parked Gandi.net registrar domain that refuses HTTPS, and no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, package or /.well-known surface survives. Surfaced originally as a Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Urban Engines
providers.description: Urban Engines was a Silicon Valley urban-mobility analytics startup founded by Shiva Shivakumar and Balaji Prabhakar that built a Space/Time Engine for analyzing how people and objects move through cities, powering commuter routing and congestion insights for cities including Washington D.C., Sao Paulo, and Singapore. Backed by a16z and GV, the company was acquired by Google in September 2016 and is now defunct; it published no public API, developer portal, or client packages, and its former website is parked on Google infrastructure.

providers.name: Quick Ride
providers.description: Quick Ride is an Indian mobility platform offering carpooling, bikepool, and taxi services across major cities including Bangalore, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, Kochi, NCR, and Chandigarh. Riders book airport, outstation, rental, and local trips across vehicle classes from hatchbacks to luxury SUVs, or share commutes via car and bike pooling to cut cost and congestion. The service is delivered through consumer iOS and Android apps. No public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP, SDKs) is published; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of prosus-ventures and enriched via live web and DNS/TLS probes.

providers.name: Aero
providers.description: Aero Technologies, Inc. is a Van Nuys, California semi-private airline founded in 2019 by Uber co-founder Garrett Camp, selling individual seats on scheduled flights and on-demand charters operated exclusively from private terminals. Its fleet comprises Embraer ERJ135 and Legacy 600 jets plus Gulfstream IV-SP aircraft, flying Los Angeles to New York City, Aspen, Sun Valley, Napa Valley, Los Cabos, Las Vegas, Maui, Miami, Heber and Greater Palm Springs. Aero distributes through aero.com, its mobile app, a travel-advisor channel, and Sabre GDS under airline designator 5E with plating carrier 307. It is a consumer travel brand: no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Baton
providers.description: Baton is a supply-chain and logistics technology company that operates as Ryder System's Silicon Valley innovation lab following its 2022 acquisition. Founded in 2019 out of 8VC's build program, Baton originally built a network of freight "drop zones" that let long-haul truckers hand off loads for local pickup and delivery, coordinating vehicles, drop zones, warehouses, and local drivers. Today the team builds RyderShare, a collaborative logistics platform combining real-time supply-chain visibility with exception management across shipments in transit. As of this enrichment pass, baton.io publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or integration surface (the site exposes only marketing and careers pages); this profile is maintained for network discovery.

providers.name: Carpooling
providers.description: Carpooling.com GmbH was one of Europe's largest ridesharing / carpooling platforms, founded in Munich, Germany and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It connected drivers with empty seats to passengers travelling the same route across Europe. In April 2015 the company was acquired by the French ridesharing operator BlaBlaCar and its operations were merged into that platform. The carpooling.com domain and every developer-facing subdomain (developer / api / docs) now redirect to BlaBlaCar (blablacar.co.uk), and no independent Carpooling developer portal, API, or specification remains. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record; there is no live API surface of its own to enrich.

providers.name: Con-way
providers.description: Con-way Inc. was a North American freight transportation and logistics company best known for its Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) carrier Con-way Freight along with Menlo Logistics, Con-way Truckload, and Con-way Multimodal. On October 30, 2015, XPO Logistics completed a $3 billion acquisition of Con-way; by May 2017 the Con-way brand had been fully retired in favor of XPO. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Con-way no longer operates under this name and modern shipping APIs are surfaced under XPO.

providers.name: Damon Motorcycles
providers.description: Damon Motorcycles (Damon Inc.) is a Vancouver, British Columbia electric motorcycle company founded in 2017 by Jay Giraud and Dominique Kwong, and an alumnus of the Techstars accelerator. Damon builds high-performance electric motorcycles led by the HyperSport and HyperFighter models, and is known for two safety and ergonomics technologies: CoPilot, a 360-degree advanced warning system that uses radar, cameras, and sensors to alert riders to surrounding hazards, and Shift, a transformable ergonomics system that adjusts the riding position between commuter and sport stances. The company has faced significant financial and going-concern difficulties, and its public web presence at damon.com currently returns errors, so no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be verified during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Enhanced Radar
providers.description: Enhanced Radar is a San Francisco-based applied AI company building intelligent systems for aviation, the world's most complex transportation domain. Its work centers on pilot-controller communications, where the company owns the full pipeline from data collection through in-house labeling and quality assurance to produce high-quality aviation AI training datasets. Products include Pattern, an aviation operational intelligence platform; ATC.com, a live air traffic control radio service; and Y4, an aviation understanding model announced in February 2026. Enhanced Radar has demonstrated real-time detection of runway incursion risks and raised $7 million in May 2026. It is backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: FlightCar
providers.description: FlightCar was a United States peer-to-peer car-rental marketplace built around airport travel, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company behind the name and no API surface of any kind. The domain flightcar.com is registered but publishes no A, AAAA or MX records, resolves to no host, and sits on Njalla privacy nameservers with a SOA serial dated 2026-07-18; the api, developer and docs subdomains do not resolve; there is no GitHub organisation at github.com/flightcar; and no first-party client library exists on npm or PyPI. The Internet Archive shows the consumer site returning 200 through May 2016 and an Internal Server Error by July 2017, with no successful captures in 2017 or 2018. FlightCar is therefore carried in the network as a defunct company retained for portfolio-graph and historical continuity rather than as an active API provider, and should not be re-queued for artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Full Truck Alliance
providers.description: Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. (Manbang Group / 满帮集团, NYSE: YMM) operates a leading digital freight platform in China that connects truckers and shippers to make road transportation more efficient. It runs the Yunmanman (运满满) and Huochebang (货车帮) mobile apps, applying mobile internet, big data, and artificial intelligence to freight matching, brokerage, transaction services, and value-added offerings across hundreds of cities and tens of thousands of routes. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures, hongshan, and softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or open platform on its corporate site; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Hawaiian Holdings
providers.description: Hawaiian Holdings was the parent company of Hawaiian Airlines, the largest and longest-serving airline of Hawaii, providing scheduled passenger service to destinations across the Pacific. In 2024 the company combined with Alaska Air Group, and Hawaiian Holdings became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alaska Air Group. No public developer portal or production-facing APIs are advertised.

providers.name: Iomob
providers.description: Iomob (The Internet of Mobility) was a Barcelona-based Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) technology company founded in 2017. Its platform let cities, transport operators, and corporations orchestrate multimodal, door-to-door journeys — combining public transit, ride-hailing, taxis, micromobility, parking, and demand-responsive transport — through unified journey-planning APIs, native iOS/Android SDKs, and customizable white-label apps. Iomob's MaaS platform and SDK were acquired by Busup in January 2025 to build a corporate mobility platform; the Iomob UK entity was dissolved in September 2025 and the public website (iomob.net) is currently offline (Cloudflare 526 origin error). No public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK packages, or GitHub organization could be verified during enrichment — Iomob's APIs and SDKs were delivered under B2B/partner agreements.

providers.name: Kansas City Southern
providers.description: Kansas City Southern (KCS) was a transportation holding company that operated freight rail networks across the United States and Mexico. On April 14, 2023, KCS merged with Canadian Pacific Railway to form Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC), the first single-line rail network connecting Canada, the United States, and Mexico. CPKC operates approximately 32,000 km (20,000 mi) of rail and is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, with U.S. headquarters in Kansas City, Missouri.

providers.name: Kyte
providers.description: Kyte was a full-stack technology-operations company that delivered rental cars on demand to the customer's door, positioning itself for any trip longer than a rideshare — a car for a day, a few days, or longer — with no rental counters, no lines and no paperwork. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company combined a consumer mobile and web booking experience with its own fleet and delivery operations ("bits and atoms"), and at its peak operated in 14 US markets delivering tens of thousands of trips per month. It was a growth-stage portfolio company of Anthemis under that firm's Data, Tech and Infrastructure thesis. Kyte was a consumer-facing operator and never published a public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal, and as of this enrichment pass its web properties no longer serve the company.

providers.name: Luxe
providers.description: Luxe was an on-demand valet parking service that let users request a valet through a mobile app to pick up, park, and return their vehicle, operating in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Luxe is a consumer mobility service with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: Meridianfleetservices
providers.description: Meridian Fleet Services is a holding company that acquires and partners with exceptional fleet service businesses, positioning itself as a permanent home for them. It focuses on preserving each acquired company's legacy and culture while supporting long-term organic growth through stronger teams, better planning and tooling, and scalable operational systems. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirmed a marketing website only (About, FAQs, Contact) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or programmatic surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: mobike
providers.description: Mobike (Chinese 摩拜单车 / 摩拜科技, "Mobike Technology") was a Beijing-based dockless bicycle-sharing company founded in 2015. Riders located, unlocked, and paid for GPS smart-lock bikes through a mobile app and QR codes. Mobike was acquired by Meituan in 2018 and its standalone brand was subsequently folded into Meituan Bike; the public site (www.mobike.com) is now a bare ICP-filing landing page with no developer API, SDK, documentation, or portal surface. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Penske
providers.description: A diversified transportation services conglomerate operating truck leasing, logistics, automotive retail, and professional motorsports across North America. Penske Corporation spans Penske Truck Leasing (full-service leasing, rental, and contract maintenance), Penske Logistics (supply chain management, warehousing, distribution, dedicated contract carriage), Penske Automotive Group (retail automotive dealerships in the US, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), and Team Penske (motorsports). The corporate parent has 73,000+ employees and approximately $43B+ in consolidated revenue. Customer self-service is delivered through web and mobile portals (Penske Fleet Insight, Penske Truck Leasing app, Penske Truck Rental); Penske does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal. Penske Automotive Group is the publicly traded subsidiary (NYSE - PAG).

providers.name: Phantom Auto
providers.description: Phantom Auto was a Mountain View, California and Ra'anana, Israel teleoperation company founded in 2017 by Shai Magzimof (CEO) and Elliot Katz (CBO) that built a remote-driving and remote-operation platform letting a human operator monitor and drive a vehicle from thousands of miles away over bonded commercial cellular links. It launched aimed at robotaxis and self-driving trucks as a safety fallback for autonomous vehicles, then pivoted in 2019 to logistics — remotely operated forklifts and yard trucks that have no autonomy of their own, plus autonomous sidewalk delivery robots — and signed customers including Maersk, CJ Logistics, ArcBest and Serve Robotics. It raised roughly $95M in total from Bessemer Venture Partners, Maniv Mobility, InfraBridge and strategic investors ArcBest and ConGlobal, closing a $25M round in 2023, and acquired Swedish low-latency video streaming company Voysys AB in October 2022. Phantom Auto ceased operations on 12 March 2024 after a funding round fell through, laying off its roughly 100-120 remaining employees. The company published no developer portal, public API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest or agent card) while it operated, and its primary host phantom.auto no longer resolves in DNS at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Pluto Mobility
providers.description: Pluto Mobility is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: mobility. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Remora
providers.description: Remora is a carbon-capture startup (legally Echeneidae Inc.) founded in 2020 and based in Wixom, Michigan, that retrofits semi-trucks and locomotives with zero-backpressure devices which extract and purify up to 90 percent of the CO2 from vehicle exhaust while cutting other pollutants. The company then sells the captured, purified carbon dioxide and shares the resulting revenue with the transportation operators it partners with. Remora is a hardware and climate-technology business with no public API or developer platform; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company for portfolio and discovery purposes.

providers.name: Riide
providers.description: Riide manufactures connected electric bicycles combining a street-legal 500W ebike (the Riide 2) with built-in GPS tracking, 4G cellular connectivity, remote lock/disable theft prevention, and a removable battery with state-of-charge monitoring. The company pairs hardware with a mobile app and connected-vehicle services. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass the public site is a consumer product/pre-order page ("coming soon") with no documented developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rimac
providers.description: Rimac Group is a Croatia-based holding company bringing together exclusive hypercars and advanced electrification technology. Its portfolio spans Bugatti Rimac (the hypercar joint venture behind the all-electric Rimac Nevera), Rimac Technology (design, engineering and production of EV components — battery systems, powertrains, battery management systems and electronic control units supplied to OEMs including Porsche, Hyundai, BMW and others), and Verne (autonomous urban mobility / robotaxi). Rimac is a B2B automotive and electrification supplier and vehicle manufacturer; it does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Ruedata
providers.description: Ruedata (RueData AI) is an AI predictive tire-management software platform for commercial fleet operators. It combines a smart digital inspection app, the TLGX precision tire-measurement device (tread depth to +/-1/32nd and pressure to +/-0.25 percent), and a centralized web platform to help fleets prevent tire blowouts, cut maintenance costs, extend tire lifecycle, and improve road safety. Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Skip Scooters
providers.description: Skip Scooters (operated by Skip Transport / Waybots) was a San Francisco-based dockless shared electric scooter (micromobility) startup and one of the early operators permitted in San Francisco, also running fleets in Washington, D.C. Backed by Accel, the company wound down and its assets moved to Helbiz around 2020. It is no longer operating: its former consumer app and rider domains (rideskip.com is a parked for-sale domain, skip.com now resolves to an unrelated retailer) have no live developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record; the enrichment pipeline found no public API to harvest.

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Superpedestrian
providers.description: Superpedestrian was a Cambridge, Massachusetts micromobility company founded in December 2012 by MIT Senseable City Lab co-inventor Assaf Biderman. It built the Copenhagen Wheel electric bicycle retrofit (2017) and then the LINK shared e-scooter fleet (2020), whose differentiator was an onboard Vehicle Intelligence System running self-diagnostic safety checks on every ride. It raised roughly $185M (a $60M round in December 2020 and a $125M Series C in February 2022 with Citi Impact Fund and Sony Innovation Fund) and at its 2022 peak ran shared fleets in about 57 cities across eleven US states and seven European countries. Superpedestrian closed its US operations on 31 December 2023 and auctioned more than 20,000 scooters in January 2024; the European business was sold to Norway's SURF Beyond in February 2024 and subsequently folded into ZEUS Mobility. The company published no public developer program and no machine-readable API contract. Its only known machine-readable surface was per-city GBFS feeds served for host cities at mds.linkyour.city, which are offline. Both superpedestrian.com and link.city are now parked domains that answer HTTP 200 to every path with a domain-parking lander, and link.city is delegated to afternic.com nameservers and listed for sale.

providers.name: TakeWheels
providers.description: TakeWheels (branded "Wheels", operated by Wheels Labs) was a shared electric micromobility platform based in Los Angeles, founded in 2018, that offered seated pedal-assist e-bikes and dockless light electric vehicles for short-distance urban trips. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital, which participated in the company's 2019 Series A. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable developer surface for this company. As of this pass the primary domain (takewheels.com) no longer resolves to the company: it issues a 301 redirect to an unrelated third-party site, indicating the business is defunct and the domain has been repurposed. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no active API surface.

providers.name: The Boring Company
providers.description: The Boring Company is an American infrastructure and tunnel-construction company founded by Elon Musk in 2016 that designs and builds underground transportation, utility, and freight tunnels to reduce urban traffic congestion. Its Prufrock tunnel-boring machines dig low-cost tunnels roughly a mile a week, and its all-electric, zero-emissions Loop system carries passengers in Tesla vehicles through those tunnels — the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop is its first commercial deployment. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its web presence is marketing, careers, Vegas Loop ticketing, and a merchandise store.

providers.name: Trinity Industries
providers.description: Trinity Industries, Inc. is a leading manufacturer and lessor of railcars in North America, providing products and services to the industrial, energy, transportation, and construction sectors. The company designs, manufactures, leases, and manages railcars used to transport commodities such as energy products, agricultural goods, construction materials, and consumer staples. Trinity operates a lease fleet of over 140,000 owned and managed railcars through its TrinityRail division.

providers.name: Vamo
providers.description: Vamo was a San Francisco travel startup offering multi-city trip planning that automatically found the best combination of open-jaw flights, low-cost carriers, trains, buses, ferries, and hotels for international itineraries. Backed by DCVC and Slow Ventures, the team joined Airbnb on September 11, 2015 and the product was shut down, so no API surface exists; vamo.com is now parked at MarkMonitor.

providers.name: Yetcargo
providers.description: Yetcargo is a Mexican freight and cargo transportation company that connects businesses needing to move goods with a network of reliable carriers, handling both local and long-distance (foráneo) shipments. Operating a Spanish-language web platform, it positions itself as a trusted cargo-transport provider ("Tu proveedor confiable de transporte de carga") for shippers who need to resolve local and out-of-town delivery problems. Yetcargo was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Zagster
providers.description: Zagster was a venture-funded bike-share startup based in Boston, Massachusetts (a Techstars portfolio company) that designed, built, and operated bike-sharing programs for cities, universities, corporate campuses, hotels, and residential communities across the United States, peaking at more than 200 programs in 2019. The company ceased bike-share operations in June 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic and is now defunct. Its former developer API host (zapi.zagster.com/api/v1/bikeshares) no longer resolves, and zagster.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Landstar System
providers.description: Landstar System is a worldwide, asset-light provider of integrated transportation management solutions delivering safe, specialized transportation services to a broad range of customers.

providers.name: Ofo
providers.description: Ofo (Chinese: 小黄车, "little yellow bike") was a Beijing dockless bicycle-sharing company founded in 2014 by Dai Wei and four classmates from the Peking University cycling club, and launched publicly on 7 September 2015. At its 2017 peak it had deployed more than 10 million bicycles across roughly 250 cities in 20 countries, reported over 60 million monthly active users, and was valued at around US$2 billion; in March 2018 it raised an $866M round led by Alibaba. Ofo's bikes were unlocked exclusively through its own consumer iOS and Android app. The company never operated a developer portal, never published a machine-readable API contract, and never shipped official client SDKs — the only documentation of its endpoints is third-party reverse-engineering of the private mobile-app API at one.ofo.com. Ofo withdrew from most international markets in July 2018, collapsed under a deposit-refund backlog that left more than 10 million users queuing for refunds from December 2018, and had ceased bike-rental operations by 2020. ofo.com is still registered through Alibaba Cloud and still resolves, but its origin refuses connections on ports 80 and 443; the historic ofo.so host dropped and was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2025 and now serves a parked arcade-game lander. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Howmet Aerospace
providers.description: Howmet Aerospace is a global leader in advanced engineered solutions for the aerospace and transportation industries, providing engine components, fastening systems, engineered structures, and forged wheels.

providers.name: Penske Automotive
providers.description: Penske Automotive Group is a Fortune 500 diversified international transportation services company that operates automotive and commercial truck dealerships principally in the United States, Canada, and Western Europe. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: RXO
providers.description: RXO is a freight and logistics platform that connects shippers and carriers across truckload, less-than-truckload, managed transportation, and last-mile delivery. The company operates RXO Connect, a digital freight platform that uses machine learning and AI across a network of approximately 150,000 independent carriers. RXO does not currently publish a public developer API portal on its corporate website.

providers.name: Allegiant Travel
providers.description: Allegiant Travel Company is a leisure-focused U.S. airline holding company and a Fortune 1000 firm operating Allegiant Air, which provides low-cost, mostly nonstop flights between underserved cities and popular leisure destinations. The company also bundles air travel with hotels, rental cars, and event tickets through its allegiant.com booking platform. Allegiant does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: JetBlue Airways
providers.description: JetBlue Airways is a low-cost airline that operates flights to destinations across the United States, Caribbean, Latin America, and Europe, known for its customer service and inflight amenities.

providers.name: Adams Resources & Energy
providers.description: Adams Resources & Energy is a diversified energy company engaged in the marketing, transportation, terminalling, and storage of crude oil and other related petroleum products in select markets across the United States. Through its subsidiaries GulfMark Energy, Firebird Bulk Carriers, Phoenix Oil, and Victoria Express Pipeline, the company purchases approximately 90,000 barrels per day at the wellhead and operates over 260 tractor-trailers and 112 pipeline inventory locations. Adams Resources & Energy serves multiple U.S. petroleum basins including the Gulf Coast, Eagle Ford Shale, Permian Basin, Bakken Shale, and Michigan, with over $1 billion in annual revenues and 400+ employees.

providers.name: Crestwood Equity Partners
providers.description: Crestwood Equity Partners LP was a master limited partnership that owned and operated midstream energy assets across the United States, including natural gas, NGL, and crude oil gathering, processing, storage, and transportation businesses. Crestwood was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in November 2023, with Crestwood common and preferred units ceasing trading on the NYSE on November 3, 2023; ongoing operations and partner contracts have been integrated into Energy Transfer's pipeline and midstream network. Crestwood does not publish a public developer API program; technical interfaces such as nominations, scheduling, and capacity portals are now handled through Energy Transfer's commercial systems.

providers.name: dstzc
providers.description: dstzc (地上铁, DiShangTie Green Technology, Shenzhen) is a leading Chinese provider of digitalized operations-management solutions for new-energy (electric) logistics vehicles. It operates a full-lifecycle fleet platform covering vehicle sales and leasing, digital fleet management, safety and risk management, maintenance, charging and battery-swap services, and residual-value management, reporting 224,000+ operational vehicles across 3,246 service locations spanning all 333 prefecture-level regions of mainland China. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company has no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Electio
providers.description: Electio (Electio Technologies) is a San Francisco-based, General Catalyst-backed software company building modern control-system software for energy production and transportation infrastructure. The company modernizes the legacy industrial control layers behind power generation, oil and gas, and transportation networks with next-generation software for monitoring, automation, and operational reliability. Electio is an early-stage, largely stealth company: it publishes a company website, a careers page, a contact page, and a privacy policy, but has not released a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile. This entry was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Ola Electric
providers.description: Ola Electric is an Indian electric-vehicle manufacturer building electric scooters (the S1 family), electric motorcycles (the Roadster line), and home energy solutions (Ola Shakti battery systems), all designed and produced in India around its in-house 4680 Bharat Cell and ferrite-motor technology. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a nationwide Hypercharger fast-charging network and Hyperservice center footprint across India. As a consumer EV and energy hardware manufacturer, Ola Electric publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API reference; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: PowerTap Hydrogen
providers.description: PowerTap Hydrogen Fueling Corp. is an Aliso Viejo, California hydrogen fueling technology company founded in 2020 and operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of the publicly traded PowerTap Hydrogen Capital Corp. (NEO: MOVE, OTC: MOTNF, FWB: 2K6B). PowerTap designs and deploys distributed, on-site "blue hydrogen" production and dispensing stations built on a patented small-scale steam methane reforming (SMR) platform with embedded carbon capture, converting natural gas and municipal water into high-purity hydrogen at the point of use rather than trucking it in. The modular station design is marketed as deployable in weeks instead of months, and the company positions it for heavy-duty trucking and light-vehicle refueling as well as baseload power for data centers. PowerTap technology-based stations operate at private enterprise sites and at a public station near LAX, with additional deployments cited in California, Texas, Massachusetts and Maryland. The company publishes no developer program, no API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; it is profiled here as an energy-infrastructure company, not an API provider.

providers.name: HUB Group
providers.description: HUB is a global leader in multifunction pole design and street infrastructure, supplying over 1,000 pieces of urban infrastructure worldwide. With 20+ years of experience, HUB excels in integrating digital devices and data analytics into innovative urban solutions. Partnered with Valmont Industries, HUB delivers high-quality infrastructure for public spaces, including telecommunications poles, monopoles, steel jackets, and head frames.

providers.name: Kobo360
providers.description: Kobo360 is a Nigerian-founded, pan-African B2B digital freight marketplace and logistics technology platform headquartered in Lagos, with operations across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo, Uganda, and other African countries. Founded in 2017 by Obi Ozor and Ife Oyedele II, Kobo360 operates an "Uber for trucks" long-haul logistics model that matches cargo owners and enterprise shippers with truck owners and drivers through a single digital ecosystem. The company runs the Global Logistics Operating System (G-LOS), an enterprise-grade logistics SaaS / digital freight forwarding platform that provides shipper dashboards, end-to-end shipment visibility, driver and truck ratings, embedded credit and working-capital products for carriers, and route and load optimization across the Kobo network of registered drivers and trucks. Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Kobo360 does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open developer portal; integrations with shippers and partners are delivered through enterprise onboarding rather than a self-service API program.

providers.name: ITT
providers.description: ITT Inc. is a diversified leading manufacturer of highly engineered critical components and customized technology solutions for the transportation, industrial, and oil and gas markets.

providers.name: Estes Energy
providers.description: Estes Energy is a US-based manufacturer of advanced battery packs for heavy-duty transport. Its magnesium-alloy Magnus platform (proprietary MgCarbonit thermo-structural body) delivers roughly 225 Wh/kg for rail, marine, aviation and off-highway applications, with chemistry-agnostic (sodium, LFP, nickel) packs manufactured entirely in the United States. Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: Enghouse
providers.description: Enghouse Systems Limited (TSX: ENGH) is a publicly traded Canadian enterprise software and services company headquartered in Markham, Ontario and founded in 1984. It builds mission-critical, communications-focused software delivered on-premise and via the cloud, organized into two segments: the Interactive Management Group (Enghouse Interactive — omnichannel contact centre, customer experience, IVR, video collaboration and AI-assisted agent tooling) and the Asset Management Group (Enghouse Networks — telecom OSS/BSS, media and broadcast, and network monitoring; plus transportation, public-safety and transit systems). The company grows largely through acquisition of specialized software brands.

providers.name: ClearFlame Engines
providers.description: ClearFlame Engine Technologies was a Woodridge, Illinois clean-combustion engine startup founded in 2016 by BJ Johnson and Julie Blumreiter, developing a retrofit technology that let conventional heavy-duty diesel engines run on ethanol and other low-carbon liquid fuels for the hard-to-electrify segments of transportation — long-haul trucking, agriculture, construction and other non-road diesel applications. It raised roughly $50M across Series A and B rounds from venture and industrial investors including John Deere, and appeared on secondary markets such as Forge Global. The company is a hardware and powertrain engineering business with no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable specifications; by 2025 it had lost investor support, its co-founder CEO had departed, it was listed as not in good standing in Illinois, and it moved toward bankruptcy and asset liquidation. Its website no longer serves content.

providers.name: Frontier Group Holdings
providers.description: Frontier Group Holdings is the parent company of Frontier Airlines, an ultra low-cost carrier headquartered in Denver, Colorado. The airline operates an Airbus A320-family fleet serving destinations across the United States, Mexico, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. No public self-service developer API or developer portal has been identified; airline distribution and partner integrations are typically handled through GDSs, NDC channels, and direct travel-agent agreements.
